text:
hannah park: Hey team — just got my M2 Max studio and doing first-boot. Kandji enrollment started but stalled at 'Completing post-enroll tasks'. Now when I try to install Rosetta I get: "Rosetta installation failed: a system extension is required" and the installer prompts for an admin password I don't have. Need to run a couple of intel-only CLI tools for my first-day demo. Who can help with a temp sudo or a recommended workaround?

kevin - IT: Welcome @hannah park! We can grant short-lived admin while we validate profile state. Pinging @it-help-bot. Before that, can you paste `profiles status -type enrollment` output and `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep 'Serial'`? Also a screenshot of the Rosetta error helps.

it-help-bot: Opening ticket INC-2026-22299. Hannah: please run the commands Kevin asked for. Also, don't attempt to disable SIP or boot to recovery unless instructed.

hannah park: Serial: C02M2STU88901. `profiles status` shows Kandji profile in state: "applied" but post-enroll hook `rosetta-check` failed with exit code 74. Screenshot uploaded.

ryan - eng-sre: Exit 74 from the Rosetta installer usually means the installer couldn't load a required system helper due to a system-policy block (macOS 13+ can block unsigned components). On Apple silicon Rosetta uses an installer package that needs a helper in /usr/libexec; if MDM hasn't allowed the installer or if theres a stubbed user approval flow, it can fail. We can do a verified temp admin install or push the official Apple Rosetta installer via Kandji.

kevin - IT: I'll approve a 45-minute temp admin window. DMing creds now. Reminder: session is logged and will auto-expire. Use it only to run the Rosetta installer and install the few CLI tools.

hannah park: Got the DM creds, ssh'd in as temp-hannah. Ran `/usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license` and got: "installer: Package name rosetta_runtime, status 74". Tried `installer -pkg /tmp/rosetta.pkg -target /` and same error.

ryan - eng-sre: Ok. Two options: 1) We push the Rosetta package via Kandji as a signed payload (preferred), or 2) we temporarily relax the policy that blocks the helper by pushing a one-off configuration allowing the Apple installer. Kevin, can Kandji push a signed pkg?

kevin - IT: Yes we can push a signed pkg. I'm going to push the official Rosetta payload now and trigger a remote command. It will show as "Rosetta installer" in Kandji and ask you to accept; it should run as root so you won't need the temp creds. Hannah, please keep the temp session open until I confirm completion.

it-help-bot: Pushed Kandji action KDJ-4521: Install Rosetta runtime. Ticket INC-2026-22299 updated.

hannah park: Kandji shows a pending command, I accepted. It started and logs show "Installation complete". Running `arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true` returns exit 0.  Success!

hannah park: Follow-up: Docker desktop installer wants an Approval for a system extension (kext) and the Security & Privacy "Allow" button is grayed out. Is that expected on an M2? I recall Apple silicon uses system extensions differently.

ryan - eng-sre: Good catch. On Apple silicon, many older kernel extensions are unsupported; Docker Desktop now uses virtualization.framework and a user-approved device management (UAM) flow. If the Allow button is grayed out it usually means the installer was run from a non-interactive context or recovery state. Did the installer run while you were in the temp admin session or as your normal user?

hannah park: I ran the Docker installer as my user right after Rosetta. The Kandji doc mentioned a UAM prompt but I don't see it.

kevin - IT: If the "Allow" button is grayed out, try this: quit System Settings, reopen and check again. If still gray, reboot once and try the install interactively (not via sudo). If that fails, DM me and we can escalate to a one-click Kandji remediation which triggers the user-approval flow.

hannah park: Rebooted, reopened System Settings, still grey. Re-running the Docker .dmg installer as my user now prompts for "Allow" and I can click it — Docker installed and runs. Phew.

dev-platform-bot: Reminder: For onboarding, generate a new ed25519 key `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "hannah.park@redwood.com"` and upload via the secure form: https://redwood.company/secrets/ssh-upload (SSO). If you need early repo access, open an access request and include the pubkey.

hannah park: Uploaded pubkey and submitted the form. Also re-generated a new GPG subkey for commit signing.

staging-printer-bot: Note: the studio has a local AirPrint queue that requires a small driver from vendor X. If you need to print from your dev machine, ping ops and we can install the user-level helper (no kext).

kevin - IT: Marking INC-2026-22299 resolved. Temp session revoked. If anything else pops up (plugin installs, Homebrew casks that need approvals) reopen the ticket. Welcome aboard, @hannah park! :tada:
